resources.string: Safer Lockscreen

While the device is locked, Safer Lockscreen watches for the Quick Settings panel, the notification shade, and the power menu, then dismisses them or locks the phone. It looks only at system-window identity: window titles, types, class names, and view ids. It does not read notification text, messages, or passwords, does not take screenshots, and does nothing after you unlock.
Blocks lock-screen Quick Settings, the notification shade, and the power menu.

Safer Lockscreen uses device admin only to lock the screen (force-lock) when Quick Settings or the power menu opens while the phone is locked. It cannot wipe the device, reset your PIN, or change your password.
Turning off device admin disables force-lock. Quick Settings blocking that depends on locking the phone will stop working until you enable it again.
Protection active
Protection incomplete

Setup needed
While this phone is locked, pulling down Quick Settings is blocked. The power menu is handled according to the toggles below. After you unlock, everything works normally.
Accessibility is on, but force-lock needs device admin. Dismiss and the top-edge block can still run. Enable device admin to finish Auto or Force lock.
Permissions are granted. Turn on protection when you want the lock screen guarded.

Enable the accessibility service. That is how the app can see the shade and power menu and close them. Android shows a system warning because this service can observe windows. The description on that screen is what this app actually does.
Force lock needs device admin. Enable it, or switch the method to Dismiss shade.
Set a PIN, pattern, or password. A swipe-only lock screen is not a lock, and force-lock cannot hold the phone without one.

Stock Pixel Android still lets anyone pull down Quick Settings on the lock screen and toggle airplane mode, Wi-Fi, or mobile data. The Android 17 “Lock Quick Settings connectivity” setting only freezes a few tiles. This app blocks the shade itself.
Set up
1. Device admin
Allows force-lock only. There is no wipe, no password reset, and no remote control. You can turn it off here before you uninstall.
Enable device admin
Device admin enabled
Deactivate device admin
2. Accessibility
Used to recognize the lock-screen shade, Quick Settings, and power menu, then dismiss them. It does not read notification contents, does not log keystrokes, and does not take screenshots.
Open accessibility settings
Accessibility enabled
If the switch is disabled, open App info, choose the menu, and tap Allow restricted settings. Then come back and enable Safer Lockscreen.
3. Protection
Block lock-screen panels
Master switch. When this is off, Quick Settings and the power menu are left alone.
Block Quick Settings on the lock screen
Closes the notification shade and Quick Settings while the phone is locked.
Block power menu on the lock screen
Closes the power-off and restart menu. The lock-screen Emergency button still works. The power button shortcut into that menu may be interrupted.
Block method
Auto
Covers the top edge so the shade swipe does not start, closes the panel if it still appears, and force-locks if the panel stays open. Recommended for Pixel.
Dismiss shade
Closes the shade or power menu when it appears. On some Pixel builds this is too slow on its own and the tiles can flash.
Force lock
Turns the screen off as soon as the panel appears. Android then asks for your PIN, pattern, or password once. Biometrics are skipped until that succeeds.
This phone has no PIN, pattern, or password. Set one in system Settings. Without it, a lock screen does not stop someone who has the phone.
Smart Lock and Extend Unlock count as unlocked. This app stays out of the way so your own Quick Settings keep working. Protection applies when Android still requires authentication (isDeviceLocked).
Limitations

The shade or power menu can flash briefly before it closes. Gesture timing differs by Android and OEM build. Emergency calling from the lock-screen Emergency button is left alone, and force-lock is paused while the emergency dialer is open, so that path can sometimes still reach Quick Settings. This is not a replacement for a strong screen lock.
Privacy

No internet permission. No ads, analytics, crash reporting, or accounts. Nothing is sent off the phone, and nothing is shared with other apps. Settings stay in device-protected storage so protection can arm after a reboot, before the first unlock. Backup is disabled.
Turn it off or uninstall
Deactivate device admin here, or in Settings, Security, Device admin apps. Then turn the accessibility service off under Settings, Accessibility. Android will not uninstall an active device admin.
Lock screen now
Checks force-lock. The screen turns off, and the next unlock asks for your PIN, pattern, or password.
